blocks.text: Navigating Slack for virtual assistants on Mac

As a virtual assistant, you likely juggle several workspaces simultaneously. The Slack desktop app for Mac makes this easier if you master the keyboard. Press Command + K to open the quick switcher. Type the name of a channel or a person to jump there instantly. This saves you from clicking through the sidebar for every request.

If you are lost, press Command + / to see the full list of shortcuts. You can also use Command + G to open the general search bar. Use search modifiers like from:name or in:channel to narrow your results. This is helpful when a client asks for a file sent three weeks ago.
Using Lazur to manage your Slack workload

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you handle your daily tasks. Hold Option + Command while looking at a Slack conversation. Ask Lazur where a setting is or how to perform a specific action. Lazur will circle the button or menu item you need. This is useful when you are learning a new client workspace.

You can also use Lazur to draft messages. Hold the fn key and dictate your response. Lazur formats the text and places it at your cursor. It is faster than typing when you have a long update to send. You can also ask Lazur to summarize a long thread. It will read the screen and give you the key points out loud.
Essential Slack tips for the daily grind

items: Use Shift + Enter to add a line break to your message without sending it.
Mark messages as unread by right-clicking them or using the three dots menu. This ensures you do not forget to reply.
Pin important messages to a channel so your clients can find them later.
Use /dnd to set your status to Do Not Disturb when you need deep focus time.
Clear your app cache via Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart if the app behaves strangely.

blocks.text: Handling multiple clients on a Mac

Managing multiple clients often leads to notification overload. Go to Preferences by pressing Command + ,. Adjust your notification settings for each workspace. You can pause notifications during specific hours. This keeps your focus on the current client.

Use different browser profiles or spaces if you use the web version of Slack. This keeps your client sessions separate. It prevents you from accidentally posting in the wrong workspace. Always double-check the workspace name in the top left corner before you send a sensitive message.
Common mistakes and how to avoid them

Many assistants forget to use threads. Threads keep your channel clean. If you reply to a message, always click the reply icon. This keeps the main channel feed readable. Another mistake is ignoring the status feature. Set your status to show when you are in a meeting. This manages client expectations about your availability.

faq.question: How do I switch workspaces in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Press Command + K to open the quick switcher and type the workspace or channel name. You can also click the workspace icons in the far left sidebar.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me write Slack messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key to dictate your message, and Lazur will type it at your cursor. It is great for drafting long updates or responses.

faq.question: How do I find a specific file in Slack?
faq.answer: Use Command + G to open the search bar. Use modifiers like has:file or from:client-name to find the exact item you need.

faq.question: What should I do if Slack is slow?
faq.answer: Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often resolves performance issues in the desktop app.
